items.title: George Wein — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Where do you see the audience gravitating or are they gravitating in one way or another?

You go down to the Jazz Gallery, it only seats about eighty people, it's packed. You go to Village Vanguard, it's packed. You go to Brooklyn and the little clubs out there, they're packed. I go listening to groups … I go listen … I had Darcy James' Band, John Hollenbeck. I'm going out listening to these people. If what they're doing, they do well, I'm interested. They don't do it well then that's another story.

Looking backwards again, as an example for audience surprises or non-surprises, you did some shows … things at the Apollo. Inexpensive tickets, right in Harlem, and the audience was not there for some tried-and-true big jazz names, whether it was – I don't remember – Carmen McRae or …
